messages:
sasha: quick follow-up to the lease/ownership RFC. want to lock down a few behavioral details before we merge the branch.
ran: go for it. which parts are still fuzzy?
sasha: three bullets: 1) fast-release semantics vs deferred reclaim and effect on eviction storms, 2) slab coalescing / compactness ordering for background reclaim, 3) how strict NUMA/affinity hints are (soft vs hard).
maria: on (1) we should make the release() call O(1) and avoid any sync scans. release should push a descriptor to a reclaim queue and return. background reclaimer does the heavy walking. otherwise we risk 95th pct spike on demote paths.
devon: agreed. implementation sketch: release() sets lease.flag = RELEASED, appends to per-tenant ring, bump per-tenant backlog metric, and returns. reclaimer thread drains rings with a budget. keep release path ~<200ns.
kevin: re (2) for compacting/coalescing: we need a deterministic policy so tests can assert slab layout. propose compactness_score = (fragmentation + age_penalty) and reclaimer picks low-score slabs first for coalesce.
ran: can you outline the compactness_score formula?
maria: simple to start: compactness_score = (free_bytes / slab_size) * age_factor. lower score => more fragmented/younger => less prefered? maybe invert so we pick highest score first. keep it linear for now.
devon: add tenant_priority multiplier so noisy tenants don't starve others. reclaimer picks by tenant_priority * compactness_score.
sasha: good point. we'll expose tenant_priority via quotas service. default=1, enterprise can raise.
kevin: NUMA: I keep thinking exposing NUMA as a first-class allocation param will be abused. make it a soft hint in flags, runtime may relocate. API: lease_acquire(tid, size, flags="SOFT_NUMA_LOCAL") and flags documented as advisory only.
ran: what about cross-node moves? if we migrate a slab to another GPU/node, how do handles behave?
maria: include a 64-bit lease_epoch in the handle. Move increments epoch and emits MOVE_EVENT. Runtime accepts old handles for a grace_window (seconds) for in-flight ops, after which handles return ESTALE.
devon: note: stale handles still may be referenced by CUDA streams etc. We'll keep a grace window and a per-handle refcount; stale handles allow reads until refcount==0. writes/new-allocs see ESTALE immediately.
kevin: ops question: how do we measure reclaim progress so SRE can alert on reclamation lag?
sasha: expose metrics: tenant_resident_bytes, lease_queue_len, reclaim_throughput_tokens, reclaim_latency_p50/p95. also push per-tenant reclaim_backpressure gauge when queue_len > soft_threshold.
ran: test plan?
maria: add unit + stress tests: fast-path-release microbench (<200ns), forced-queue reclaim path, tenant-move while reclaim in-flight, fuzz with concurrency. Also add deterministic coalesce test that seeds known fragmentation pattern and asserts final slab counts.
devon: I'll add a small harness in runtime/integration that can run with --fuzz-reclaim and random pauses to hit races.
kevin: one more: isolation model. default soft-sharing with quotas; but Dedicated enterprise customers can enable strict islandization. when islandized, cross-tenant transfer of slabs is forbidden and reclaim will never steal under their quota.
sasha: agreed. action items: 1) update RFC with API snippet + advisory flag semantics, 2) maria/devon to draft compactness_score formula and pseudo-code, 3) kevin/ops to enumerate metrics and thresholds for alerts, 4) ran to add test matrix. return with updates EOD tomorrow.
ops-bot: CI: lease-epoch-refactor branch passed unit tests (CI #3781) :white_check_mark:
ran: ack. i'll review the NUMA hint wording.
maria: drafting compactness formula now.
devon: will add fuzz harness and ticket the tests.
kevin: will document islandization edge cases and migration policy.
sasha: thanks all. ping me if you hit an unclear edge in migration path.
